key_insight: Adaptive optimization of discrete PDE losses can identify highly accurate self-similar singularity profiles without prescribing far-field amplitudes.
engineering_relevance: The approach offers computational scientists a high-accuracy tool for studying PDE blow-up while avoiding finite-domain truncation.
method: Represent fields with overlapping local Chebyshev patches and a mapped asymptotic patch.
Factor out leading power laws and optimize the remaining profiles, including limiting amplitudes at infinity.
Refine using Chebyshev-coefficient decay and solve with automatically differentiated Gauss–Newton iterations and Levenberg–Marquardt damping.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports O(10^-14)-level accuracy for Burgers profiles, residuals of O(10^-14)–O(10^-10) for generalized De Gregorio equations, and O(10^-8) residuals in a local region for 2D Boussinesq equations.
watch_item: Small numerical residuals, especially in a local region, do not alone establish a rigorous global PDE singularity.
paper_title: Discovery of Singularities in Partial Differential Equations Using Adaptive Numerical Discretizations
